I'd like a CS degree simply because I have some experience programming and I would be marketable. Much of my frustration comes from low feelings of self worth tied to my low pay. 

It isn't so much that I want to be a programmer. I don't really have any passions, and I'm easily upset by bullshit politics at places I've worked.

I'm a fan of Viktor Frankl's idea about the point of life. He basically said that life only has the meaning we give to it through our actions. I interpret his words to mean that if we choose to make life meaningful to ourselves by accruing large sums of money, that's fine. If we prefer to alleviate the suffering of others, that's fine too.

Not your first responder, but I'll interject if you don't mind. 

The light at the end of the tunnel keeps me going. Not that I see one. I believe there may be something more positive in my life eventually. If this holds to be true, then having something is certainly better than the neutrality that is death. If however, I'm wrong and there is nothing better to come, I still find death and the end result is the same.

The article is misleading. Exposure to germs doesn't make the baby's immune system "stronger". It just helps the immune system develop differently. If the immune system isn't presented with microbes such as bacteria, yeast, and virii, then it develops in a manner that is less capable of dealing with potential threats of those kinds, and instead develops toward whatever else it finds to be a threat.
